messages:
Emily Chen: Heads-up — Northwind is asking for a Private deployment that must be air-gapped and want pricing aligned to our Dedicated commit tiers. they explicitly said no back-channel telemetry and a 36-month no-egress covenant. how do we structure this without making it a full custom SOW?
Maya Ortiz: Sales perspective: big strategic account. They hate unpredictable overruns. they'd prefer a committed SKU model (GPU-hour equivalent) plus a named support band. if we force a massive one-time engineering pass, they might walk.
Leo Zhang: Engineering: air-gapped Private + reserved GPUs is supported but we need extra automation for offline package delivery and a hardened upgrade path. maintenance burden adds ~25% ongoing cost. streaming, webhook callbacks and remote config will need offline alternatives.
Raj Patel: Solutions: we can do a "Compliance Pack" add-on SKU. Options: (A) flat monthly surcharge; (B) per-node airgap agent license; (C) blended commit model: annual GPU commit + per-node maintenance fee. Blended seems closest to customer ask.
Nina Brooks (Finance): Financial constraints: flat surcharges compresss unit economics if we underprice. per-node maintenance is easier to model. Recommend blended: commit revenue + fixed per-node ops fee. also propose amortizing install eng hours into first-year charge.
Samir Gupta (Legal): Contract cautions: explicit no-egress covenants ok but need narrow definitions (what counts as telemetry, updates). propose an Annex with allowed maintenance windows and an opt-in list for telemetry endpoints. liability cap and indemnity carveouts must be clear for on-prem incidents.
Emily Chen: Good. Let's define launch criteria before we promise: 1) deployment automation docs + offline upgrade checklist; 2) Console feature flag to hide/disable streaming and webhook integrations per customer; 3) pricing SKU definitions and templates for Sales; 4) legal template with allowed-exceptions annex.
Leo Zhang: Engineering estimate: work items: offline package build & signing (2 sprints), Console UI toggles + quota UI (2 sprints), offline diagnostics tooling and support-runbooks (1 sprint). total ~5 sprints. If we limit initial scope (no automated agent updates) could shave 2 sprints.
Maya Ortiz: Sales asks for two pricing proposals to present: conservative (higher flat ops fee, faster SLA) and competitive (lower ops fee, tighter commit). also need example TCO comparison vs hosted.
Raj Patel: I'll produce sample pricing grid: annual GPU commit tiers mapped to our Dedicated price table, per-node maintenance ($/node/month), and optional Premium Onsite Support day rate. Also include recommended discount thresholds for multi-year commit.
Nina Brooks (Finance): Add a note: revenue recognition will differ for bundled professional services. ensure Billing knows to treat install and annual commits separately.
Samir Gupta (Legal): I'll draft a short clause for the no-egress requirement and a telemetry opt-in paragraph. also flag export-control review if customer is in EMEA regulated sector.
contract-bot: Reminder — attach NDA + upload proposed contract to ContractHub for redline.
Emily Chen: Next steps: Raj + Leo to share pricing grid and minimal runbook by EOD today, Samir to post legal starter language, Nina to sanity-check economics. Maya will present both proposals to Northwind on Wed.
Raj Patel: Roger. I'll attach a CSV pricing grid and two sample TCO scenarios here by 6pm.
Leo Zhang: I'll paste the minimal offline runbook checklist and a high-level rollout timeline (8-12 weeks depending on automation scope) by 5:30pm.
Samir Gupta (Legal): Draft clause (starter):
```
Customer shall operate Redwood Private within an isolated network environment with no outbound network communications to public internet domains, except for those telemetry endpoints explicitly enumerated and consented to in Annex A. Redwood will provide an opt-in mechanism for telemetry and will not transmit customer data to Redwood-controlled infrastructure without written approval.
```
Will add liability and maintenance exceptions.
Nina Brooks (Finance): If Northwind signs a 36-month commit, propose 8% annual discount and amortize install fees over year one. will run scenarios when Raj posts grid.
Maya Ortiz: Thanks team — this is the format Northwind needs. If we can present two clean options with clear runbook + SLA differences, we should close. :thumbsup:
